answer: A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The kernel cap is enforced at intake and inlet shows the per-origin counts. At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a lantern tag. That is 6 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
